P.text: A normal user stakes the minimum allowed amount (10 gwei), receives kHYPE, and queues a withdrawal that creates a tiny L1 operation (1 in 8 decimals); the L1 bridge rejects the tiny amount.
P.evidence_quote: Staking the minimum allowed amount (10 gwei) => Queuing a withdrawal that creates a tiny L1 operation (1 in 8 decimals) => Permanently blocking all subsequent operations when the bridge rejects the tiny amount

I.text: The StakingManager L1 operations queue should be able to skip failed operations, selectively reset the queue, retry operations, or override failures so a failed L1 operation does not irreversibly lock subsequent operations and user funds.
I.evidence_quote: When transactions in _processL1Withdrawals() or _processL1Deposits() fail, the contract cannot skip failed operations, reset the queue selectively, retry operations, or override failures.

V.text: When an L1 bridge call fails, the operation reverts and the processing index remains unchanged; because operations process sequentially, all subsequent operations become permanently stuck. When admins reset the queue, all pending withdrawal operations are deleted with no record, users' ETH remains trapped, and all users with pending withdrawals permanently lose their funds.
V.evidence_quote: When a call to l1Write.sendTokenDelegate() fails, the operation reverts and the processing index remains unchanged. Since operations process sequentially, all subsequent operations become permanently stuck.
